notes.10: This heading required candidates to provide two points by which the level of pollution would be in control. The majority of candidates were able to provide the right answers under this heading. Question 11 was about the alternative means by which commuters pay the fare. Exercise 4 Question 12 In this summary-writing exercise up to six marks are available for Content and four marks for Language. This year most candidates appear to be well-prepared for the requirements of this exercise and generally performed well. Many candidates wrote their summaries in their own words and were therefore able to access the full range of marks available for Language. Most of the candidates wrote precisely, covering five or six correct points from the text. They also managed to secure three out of four marks for language; a few candidates scored full marks for language. The majority of the candidates restricted their answer to within the word limit. However, a small minority of candidates still exceeded the word limit. Section 2 Exercise 5 Questions 13–19 This text was about a social worker who worked for the people who are working as labourers in the field of coal and limestone mining. Many of the candidates performed very well in this exercise. All of the questions ( Questions 13–16 ) with true/false options and supplying the correct statement for the false option were answered correctly by most of the candidates. From Question 17–19 , most of the candidates gave accurate statements. Some candidates gave an incorrect answer to Question 18 . The question was what ideological values did she use in her work? The correct answer was the values inherited from India. Perhaps the word ‘value’ in Hindi was not clear to some candidates. Exercise 6 This year’s essay topic was ‘Does the spirit of mutual competition affect the level of sports?’ Several candidates gave their argument in support of the topic. However, few candidates diverted their attention from the main topic and added points related to good health. Good answers gave interesting examples of competition and related their examples to the negative consequences. Similarly to last year, spelling errors were the main reason for loss of marks. Firstly, the use of the vowel sounds ‘Ee’ was used wrongly. Secondly, the aspirated letters were written with non-aspirated letters in Hindi. Thirdly, the conjunct in Hindi especially with the letter ‘Ra’ was not used correctly. Teachers should encourage their students to think in Hindi because some of the sentence constructions were written in Hindi however it sounded as if students were planning what they were writing in English and then translating their thoughts into Hindi, thereby causing problems with the syntax of their writing.
